newsitem.title: FINLAND: SHIP DELIVERY SKEWED JUNE TRADE DATA - FINLAND BANK.
newsitem.headline: SHIP DELIVERY SKEWED JUNE TRADE DATA - FINLAND BANK.

text.p: The Finnish June trade surplus released by the National Customs Board fell short of the Bank of Finland's earlier estimate mainly because of the timing of one big ship delivery, a central bank official said on Thursday.
"The difference is mainly due to one major ship delivery, which the customs had booked earlier than we did," Jorma Hilpinen, head of office of the Bank of Finland told Reuters.
Hilpinen declined to specify the value of the ship delivery, which the central bank included in its clearly bigger June export figure, which pulled up the Bank's June trade surplus.
NCB said the June trade surplus was 5.8 billion markka, up from 4.6 billion in May. The Bank of Finland had earlier estimated the June trade surplus at 7.8 billion markka.
The NCB's official monthly trade statistics are lagging behind due to changes in customs prodedures when Finland joined the European Union at the start of 1995.
The central bank's preliminary figures are based on a survey among export and import companies.
